name: Khalistan movement
summary: The Khalistan movement seeks an independent Sikh homeland in Punjab, separate from India. Scholars describe it as a secessionist, ethno-religious campaign that grew out of Sikh autonomy politics and turned into an armed insurgency in the 1980s after Operation Blue Star; today it is carried mainly by diaspora campaigners such as Sikhs For Justice, whose Punjab independence referendum claims a right to self-determination by peaceful, democratic means. It has no agreed programme on economics, government or society, and advocates have been criticised for not setting one out.
scope: The campaign for a sovereign Sikh state (Khalistan), as defined by scholarship that treats it as secessionism (Webb; Jedlinski) and as stated by Sikhs For Justice's Punjab independence referendum and the 1986 Declaration of Khalistan as reported by Gurnam Singh. Excluded as other subjects: the Shiromani Akali Dal's Anandpur Sahib Resolution and its 1978 economic and social resolutions (an autonomy platform of one party, which Webb shows moderated while separatism faded), individual armed groups' strategy, and Bhindranwale's own preaching, which Jedlinski says was not necessarily independence. Positions the defining sources do not state for the movement are left null.

notes: Later pass 2026-11-13 under rules 7. The first pass rested on Wikipedia and on the Akali Dal's Anandpur Sahib Resolution and 1978 resolutions; the defining scholarship (Webb, Jedlinski, Gurnam Singh) ties the movement to secession and says its advocates never set out governance, economic or social programmes, so those answers are now null. Answers kept rest on Sikhs For Justice's stated case for self-determination and on Webb. Themes searched: economy, government, society, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism (the Sikh Encyclopedia and Anandpur text, Sikhs For Justice's site, three scholarly or reference articles); nothing further was stated for the movement itself. Not read: the full 1986 declaration (blocked) and the book-length studies (not open access). A final search for a draft constitution or governance, minority and women's-rights programme of Khalistan found only the 'Democratic Republic of Khalistan' label and territorial map claims from Sikhs For Justice, which settle none of the statements.
